Some interesting data points:
- 3.3.0 on Debian 12 with our Python 3.14 and GCC 16.2 works.
- 3.3.0 on Debian 12 using the system Python 3.11 works.
- 3.3.0 on Ubuntu 24.04 with GCC 13.3 and our Python 3.14 works.

Can anyone shed light as to why `cython-3.3.0/Cython/Compiler/Code.c` would be different in two different builds which should be using the same Python version, specifically:

```
3727,3735d3706
< /* VoidPtrExport.proto */
< static int __Pyx_ExportVoidPtr(PyObject *api_dict, const char *name, void *p, const char *sig);
<
< /* GetApiDict.proto */
< static PyObject *__Pyx_ApiExport_GetApiDict(void);
<
< /* FunctionExport.proto */
< static int __Pyx_ExportFunction(PyObject *api_dict, const char *name, void (*f)(void), const char *sig);
```

One of these builds is cross-compiled and Python is notoriously fiddly, so I wouldn't be surprised if there is some fun edge case to be considered.

Another data point.  Debian 11, the uv-standalone python 3.14.7, cython 3.3.0 builds.  Debian 11 but using our build of python 3.14.7, cython 3.3.0 fails.

With identical versions but different builds of 3.14.7 I get that difference in `Code.c` above still. This feels important...

I argued with chatgpt for a bit and after lots of digressions it said "try a serial build".

That fixed it.

3.3.0 breaks parallel builds (passing eg `-j8` to setup.py).
Note that parallel builds made a massive difference to build time. On my machine I can build 3.2.9 with `-j` in 89.1s, but as 3.3.3 fails with `-j` it now takes 243.1s.

FWIW, ChatGPT blames the global `Options.cimport_from_pyx` being mutated in parallel builds by the shared-module code, resulting in unexpected state and thus broken builds.  No idea how accurate that is.

This is Cython building itself, right? 

I don't think we use `Options.cimport_from_pyx` when building Cython so it shouldn't be mutated.

I believe the parallel builds try to use multiprocessing rather that threading so there hopefully shouldn't be much mutated in parallel. But I know in the past setuptools has unhelpfully added some thread-based parallelism too (specifically the error tracking state in the case I remember)

My current (untested) guess is that it might be related to a GCC issue we saw with LTO (the GCC versions don't quite match for that, so I could definitely be wrong). If that was the case, it might be more to do with when a partially complete build starts to use compiled Cython. 

If that's wrong, I suspect we should add a giant global mutex around all of Cython to exclude any thread-based parallelism. It's certainly not something that we've accounted for and we really are expecting multiprocessing instead

I've occasionally seen that refnanny failure in our benchmark tests. So that's definitely known and happens to people other than you

That's good to know, at least.  Trying to isolate exactly what the trigger is for the compile failures I see more frequently in our build tool (the original error) which I can't quite replicate outside...

I can reproduce this build failure on debian12 with the distro gcc12 and uv's python 3.14.7:

```
cython/Cython/Compiler/Parsing.c: In function ‘__Pyx_modinit_Variable_export_code’:
cython/Cython/Compiler/Parsing.c:82008:686: error: ‘__pyx_v_6Cython_8Compiler_7Parsing__bytes’ undeclared (first use in this function); did you mean ‘__pyx_v_6Cython_8Compiler_7Parsing_Nodes’?
```

Can't make it happen on the same machine using system python3.11.
If you don't get an answer first, I'll try to have a proper look next week

Amazing twist.  I turned off parallel builds and sent the build to our cluster. One of the tests it does is reproducibility verification: take one build from the cache, do another build from scratch, and compare the output.  Same version of Python, same Cython,

`Cython/Compiler/FlowControl.c` changes: `PyNumberBinop.proto` appears in that file, and one line changes subtly:

```diff
-__pyx_t_8·=·__Pyx_PyNumber_InPlaceOr_int_object(__pyx_v_i_state,·__pyx_t_12);·if·(unlikely(!__pyx_t_8))·__PYX_ERR(0,·590,·__pyx_L1_error)
+__pyx_t_8·=·__Pyx_PyNumber_InPlaceOr_object_object(__pyx_v_i_state,·__pyx_t_12);·if·(unlikely(!__pyx_t_8))·__PYX_ERR(0,·590,·__pyx_L1_error)
```

The full report can be seen [here](https://valkyrie.yocto.io/pub/repro-fail/oe-reproducible-20260915-6gd413zg/packages/diff-html/#reproducibleA-tmp---reproducibleA-tmp-deploy---reproducibleA-tmp-deploy-deb---reproducibleA-tmp-deploy-deb-x------v----reproducibleA-tmp-deploy-deb-x------v--python--cython-src_-.-.--r-_amd--.deb---data.tar.xz---data.tar---.-usr-src-debug-python--cython--.-.--Cython-Compiler-FlowControl.c). We compare the final packaged output so there's a lot of changes but that is the initial difference.

> one line changes subtly

Interesting. There might be something wrong with the type inference here, possibly related to in-place operators (or annotations?). The relevant code lines from `FlowControl.py` (lines 576+) are:
```python
    block: ControlBlock
        i_state = block.i_input
            i_assmts = flow.assmts[stat.entry]
                i_state = i_state & ~i_assmts.mask
                if stat.is_deletion:
                    i_state |= i_assmts.bit
                else:
                    i_state |= stat.bit
```
According to your diff, there can apparently be cases in which `i_state` is inferred as `object`, although it should normally be inferred as Python `int`. I can't say why, needs investigation.

EDIT: This is unlikely to fail the build, though – the result of the changed operation should still be correct.

> one line changes subtly

I created https://github.com/cython/cython/issues/8002

Contrary to what I thought was intended, when run through setuptools, `cythonize` ends up being run in thread-parallel (rather than process-parallel). Within the `cythonize` function itself does have an `nthreads` argument to split things into process-parallel. However when called from `setuptools` that's `1` and `setuptools` handles the parallelism.

Practically I think there's quite a bit of global state in Cython that we can't realistically avoid. We've guarded a small amount in the `Errors.py` but I think it'd be more trouble than it's worth to try to fix.

I think I'll try to force it to spawn an isolated process in these circumstances. It's probably the easiest solution.
Shouldn't we ask setuptools to avoid this?

> Shouldn't we ask setuptools to avoid this?

I can do. Although I expect their response would be:
* They're mostly just parallelizing by  invoking `gcc` and a separate Python process to do that really is excessive.
* We could fix it in Cython by making Cython thread-safe (which is true)
* We could fix it in Cython with our custom `build_ext` command, which is also true - we'd need to override either `build_extensions()` or [`_build_extensions_parallel()`](https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/blob/4e612f9e44ecfad130d0b2a27a2dce0740599b4b/setuptools/_distutils/command/build_ext.py#L505). We'd need to make sure that `Extension` was pickleable though for a simple re-write.

To me this does feel like something that's best fixed on our side, but I can ask.
My other observation is that I don't think `old_build_ext` had this problem (because it does the Cython call as a preprocessing step behind the bit that setuptools parallelizes)

> They're mostly just parallelizing by  invoking `gcc` and a separate Python process to do that really is excessive.

Ah, ok. I wasn't aware that we're talking about Cython's `build_ext` here.

> preprocessing step behind the bit that setuptools parallelizes

We could go back to doing that. There's an overridable method `build_extensions` in distutils back to at least Py3.8 (and still in setuptools' copy) that delegates to the threaded build, so that would be a good place to hook into and run Cython before passing to the super method.

https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/blob/4e612f9e44ecfad130d0b2a27a2dce0740599b4b/setuptools/_distutils/command/build_ext.py#L492

> We could fix it in Cython by making Cython thread-safe

We should try to do that as well, but I can't say what it would take to do that.

> There's an overridable method build_extensions in distutils [...]

To me it looks reasonably easy to add `cythonize` there in series but fairly difficult to add `cythonize` there in parallel. We can't feed all the modules into a single call to `cythonize` and use our existing multi-processing mechanism because they all can have different options. Trying to parallelize it with multiprocessing in `build_extensions` requires `ext` to be pickleable (while the place we've got it in `cythonize` doesn't).

Parallelizing the C compile seems more important that parallelizing `cythonize`, but I still think parallelizing `cythonize` is a nice thing to do.

I agree about the `force_parallel` option on my existing proposal being nasty though. I think I'll try an alternative version without the extra parameter on the basis that this preserves the parallel builds.

> We can't feed all the modules into a single call to `cythonize` and use our existing multi-processing mechanism because they all can have different options.

Why is that a problem? With "options", do you mean the attributes of the Extension object or Cython's options? Both work with `cythonize()`, don't they?
Ah, sorry, I only looked it up now – our `build_ext` actually does the mapping from Extension attributes to Cython options…

> FWIW, ChatGPT blames the global `Options.cimport_from_pyx` being mutated in parallel builds by the shared-module code, resulting in unexpected state and thus broken builds. No idea how accurate that is.

In hindsight I think this probably was the main issue my search of `cimport_from_pyx` on github from my phone didn't manage to find it. Not sure it's the only bit of dubious global state in Cython but it's certainly an obvious one that's being mutate and has been changed in Cython 3.3.

> they all can have different options

There will usually be large overlaps, though. We could group the extensions by their options (`tuple(options.values())`) and run one `cythonize()` command for each set. I don't think there would be many cases with more than three runs. That seems acceptable.

> the global `Options.cimport_from_pyx` being mutated in parallel builds by the shared-module code

A fix for this was actually part of my work that I mentioned in https://github.com/cython/cython/issues/7939#issuecomment-5638251436 but couldn't finish yet. I don't think it's far off, though, so we might just wait for that. I pushed an incomplete branch if anyone wants to take a look over it:

https://github.com/cython/cython/compare/master...scoder:cython_scope_setup?expand=1

> > one line changes subtly
> 
> I created [#8002](https://github.com/cython/cython/issues/8002)

The non-determinism in type inference is hopefully fixed in https://github.com/cython/cython/pull/8025

However, I failed to reproduce the issue with a test, so I cannot tell for sure right now.

> one line changes subtly

I've taken the safe and simple path for fixing this specific issue:
https://github.com/cython/cython/commit/0a948c7d65f91690674db4c855dadce501a3181d
